sources.name: National Park Service — Public Trails (existing, official trails; mountain trails ≥0.3 mi not already listed)
sources.query: TRLNAME IS NOT NULL AND TRLNAME <> ' ' AND TRLNAME <> '' AND TRLSTATUS IN ('Existing','Exisiting') AND (ISEXTANT IS NULL OR ISEXTANT <> 'False') AND (TRLFEATTYPE IS NULL OR TRLFEATTYPE NOT IN ('Unofficial Trail','Unmaintained Trail','Unmaintained Trail Centerline')) AND (TRLTYPE IS NULL OR TRLTYPE NOT IN ('Sidewalk','Water Trail','Snow Trail','Ferry Route'))

sources.name: USGS National Transportation Dataset — Trails
sources.query: (name IS NOT NULL AND name <> '') OR hikerpedestrian = 'Y'

sources.name: OpenSkiMap — ski runs (used to identify ski runs; not listed as trails)
sources.query: U.S./Canadian pistes; a record is a run when ≥60% of its line follows a piste

sources.name: OpenStreetMap — trailheads (start points)
sources.query: highway=trailhead within 800 m of a trail end; 10,427 trails matched; OSM data as of 2026-05-06T03:25:00Z

notes: Each record is a whole named trail: 492,665 source sections were merged where sections with the same name connect (within 200 m). Same-named trails that do not connect stay separate, except named through-hikes (Appalachian, Pacific Crest, …), which are one trail even across mapping gaps. Unnamed sections are never merged.

Trail length is the sum of its sections with overlapping stretches counted once. U.S. sections use USGS-reported miles when they agree with the mapped line (within 0.67–1.5×); otherwise, and for all Canadian sections, length is measured from the generalized geometry.
Generalized source geometry is for discovery, not navigation. Map pins are points on the trail's longest mapped line, not verified trailheads.
State/province is inferred from the map pin and Natural Earth public-domain boundaries; long trails can extend outside it.
Seasonal access, overnight camping, water, difficulty and elevation are not inferred. Source data may be older than the retrieval date.
U.S. eligibility is named USGS sections plus unnamed sections tagged hikerpedestrian=Y; unnamed sections are labeled Unnamed trail.
Standalone trails shorter than 0.05 mi are mapping fragments and are excluded.

National Park Service trails are added only when NPS lists them as existing, official, open trails (not unofficial, unmaintained, sidewalk, water or snow trails) and the line is not already in the catalog. New NPS trails must be at least 0.3 mi and in mountain terrain (sampled elevation varies ≥100 m within 1 km, or the trail climbs ≥60 m; Copernicus DEM via Open-Meteo). NPS lines that fill gaps in existing trails are kept.

Every trail is checked by config/trail-quality.json rules: 94,728 passed, 20,629 are short trails, 3,422 need review and 27,649 are partial, unnamed or connector segments kept out of default results. No elevation is available from these sources.
1,531 records follow downhill ski pistes mapped in OpenSkiMap and are listed as ski runs, not hiking trails; 2,347 follow Nordic ski tracks and stay hikeable.
